newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Paranapanema unit to delist stock. [CORRECTED 23:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Brazil Paranapanema unit to delist stock. [CORRECTED 23:45 GMT]

text.p: Brazilian metals group Paranapanema said its unit Laminacao de Metais would delist its stock.

The group has requested the local Securities and Exchange Commission (CVM) to delist Laminacao de Metais' shares from the stock exchanges, said the firm's financial and Investor Relations director Helio Blak.
Paranapanema conglomerate will remain with four listed companies: Caraiba Metais, Eluma, Companhia Paraibuna de Metais and Paranapanema, which is the group's holding.
The group also said it plans to merge next year the operations of Laminacao de Metais and Eluma.

The conglomerate was formed earlier this year (Corrects from last year) after a pool of pension funds, led by Previ pension fund of government bank Banco do Brasil, took over Caraiba, Paraibuna and Paranapanema. Eluma was already controlled by the funds.
Paranapanema group reported gross revenues of 1.05 billion reais in 1995, according to the company's president Dennis Braz Goncalves.

Goncalves said this year's revenues would be lower due to a drop in commodity prices, particularly of copper, which accounts for 60 percent of the group's total receipts. He said copper's average price this year will be at least $600 below 1995's average price.
